newsitem.title: USA: AT&T pares management ahead of analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: AT&T pares management ahead of analyst meeting.

text.p: AT&T Corp will unveil a set of moves aimed at streamlining management of its core consumer and business operations in a two-day meeting with financial analysts that begins Monday, a spokeswoman said.

Held near the company's Basking Ridge, N.J. headquarters, this will be the first such meeting held under John Walter, the company's recently hired president and chief operating officer, who is slated to become AT&T chief executive in May.
Among the plans to be detailed will be initiatives to sharpen the accountability of AT&T's management and beef up corporate brand advertising, the spokeswoman said.
AT&T also will centralize marketing and other functions of two fast-growing Internet businesses under the wings of its mainline operating units, spokeswoman Adele Ambrose said.
These plans were what was behind AT&T's announcement Thursday that it would cut "several hundred" managerial jobs at various levels of the organization.

The consolidation efforts are expected to strengthen the hands of consumer marketing chief Gail McGovern and business marketing chief Jeffrey Weitzen, while reducing the scope of several other senior excutives, analysts believe.

Walter will seek to convince Wall Street that management issues which have plagued AT&T in the past year are behind it, and that he is ready to lead the company's charge into new markets opened by telecommunciations deregulation.
The cuts will be dispersed throughout the U.S. operations in "onesies and twosies," Ambrose said.
"It is not an elimination of senior managers per se," she added, although some senior managers would be reassigned as part of the plan.
AT&T officials also will describe efforts to consolidate its marketing efforts into one integrated brand strategy, incorporating advertising, sponsor and direct mail programs.

"People will be hearing how we are really beefing up the way we manage our brand-advertising strategy," Ambrose said of plans for a major new ad program. "We really are trying to 'grow the brand,' as they say in the advertising world."
Assigned to take the lead in the new brand advertising campaign will be Marilyn Laurie, the company's public relations and corporate advertising chief.
Two Internet businesses will no longer operate independently, but be folded under the command of the main consumer and business marketing operations.

These include AT&T's WorldNet Internet access service, which has grown to serve 750,000 subscribers in the one year it has been in operation, and its EasyCommerce Services unit, which helps small businesses conduct commerce on the Internet.

"They are coming out of the incubator and are moving into the big blockbuster marketing organziation," Ambrose said of a plan to tie its Internet businesses into the centralized marketing efforts for core consumer and business operations.
EasyCommerce's Web-site hosting services are acquiring the business cachet associated with the toll-free 800-number services AT&T offers its corporate customers, she said.
"The real point of these moves is not to cut jobs," the spokeswoman said. "It is to rationalize the organization to make it more in sync with the overall strategy," Ambrose said.
